name: Overhead Barbell Press
instructions: Stand tall holding barbell across front of shoulders at clavicle height.
Squeeze glutes and core firmly.
Press bar straight overhead, tucking chin slightly until bar passes forehead.
Lock out overhead with biceps by ears.
coachTips: A rigid core prevents lower back hyperextension.
breathingTip: Breathe in and brace at the bottom; exhale at the top lockout.
progressionNote: Progress with micro-plates (1.25kg) for steady shoulder gains.

name: Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Press
instructions: Sit on an upright bench with dumbbells at shoulder height, palms forward.
Press dumbbells overhead until arms are extended but not locked.
Lower with control back to ear level.
commonMistakes: Allowing lower back to arch off the backrest
coachTips: Keep bench at 80-85 degrees rather than 90 to protect the rotator cuff.
breathingTip: Inhale on descent; exhale pushing up.
progressionNote: Increase by 1-2kg per dumbbell when 3x12 is achieved.

name: Standing Dumbbell Lateral Raise
instructions: Stand with dumbbells at sides with a slight forward torso lean.
Raise arms out to sides leading with elbows until parallel to the floor.
Pause briefly at top, then lower with a controlled 2-second negative.
commonMistakes: Using momentum and shrugging shoulders up to ears
coachTips: Pour the water: tilt pinkies slightly up at the peak for maximum side delt recruitment.
breathingTip: Exhale lifting up; inhale lowering down.
progressionNote: Strict control and tempo matter far more than heavy weights here.

name: Cable Lateral Raise
instructions: Set pulley at lowest height. Stand sideways and grab handle with far hand.
Raise arm out to the side until parallel to floor.
Lower slowly under continuous cable tension.
commonMistakes: Leaning too far away from the stack
coachTips: Provides constant tension even at the bottom of the movement.
progressionNote: Increase reps to 15-20 before moving up pin weight.

name: Bent-Over Dumbbell Rear Delt Fly
instructions: Hinge forward at hips with flat back until torso is almost parallel to floor.
Hold light dumbbells beneath chest with slight elbow bend.
Raise arms out to sides squeezing the back of your shoulders.
Lower under control.
commonMistakes: Swinging upper body to lift weight
coachTips: Can be done seated on the edge of a bench to eliminate lower back fatigue.
breathingTip: Exhale as arms raise; inhale lowering.
progressionNote: Focus on feeling the burn in the rear shoulder cap.

name: Arnold Dumbbell Press
instructions: Hold dumbbells in front of chest with palms facing you (like top of bicep curl).
As you press upward, rotate palms away from you 180 degrees.
Lock out overhead with palms forward.
Reverse rotation smoothly on the way down.
coachTips: Hits anterior delts through full rotational range of motion.
breathingTip: Inhale rotating down; exhale pressing up.
progressionNote: Use lighter weights than standard shoulder presses to maintain form.

name: Pike Push-Up (Bodyweight Shoulder Builder)
instructions: Start in downward dog or pushup position, walk feet forward so hips form an inverted V.
Lower top of head toward the floor between your hands.
Press through palms to push back up into the pike position.
commonMistakes: Flaring elbows wide instead of tracking back
coachTips: Elevate feet onto a chair to scale up toward handstand pushups.
breathingTip: Inhale going down, exhale pushing up.
progressionNote: Progress by elevating feet on progressively higher surfaces.

name: Dumbbell Front Raise
instructions: Stand tall holding dumbbells in front of thighs with overhand grip.
Raise one or both arms straight out in front until eye level.
Lower slowly under control.
coachTips: Keep core braced and resist swinging.
progressionNote: Pause for a split-second at eye level.
